source.description: One eight-panel graphite-and-colored-pencil contact sheet intended to become seven cumulative process frames and one finished master after full-sheet review.
source.notes: Keep one young elephant calf in one left-facing side view with its trunk curling upward, exactly one visible near ear with the far ear hidden, four readable legs, one small visible tusk, one tail, soft skin folds, a broken ground shadow, tactile graphite, restrained blue-gray and dusty-rose pencil, and no water spray, tree, grassland scene, text, labels, arrows, numbers, signature, watermark, border, or extra animal.

process_strategy: Use eight cumulative stages so the pale pose map, head-body-trunk silhouette, legs and tail, face and anatomy landmarks, skin texture and shadow, graphite value, restrained colored pencil, and final reinforcement each have one distinct visible job. Reserve the visible near-ear overlap, all four leg routes, the tusk, eye, trunk opening, tail, highlights, and ground shadow before dark contours or value so no keeper line must be erased later.

final_elements.name: pale elephant pose anatomy highlight and shadow map
final_elements.description: Light graphite places the head and body masses, upward trunk route, two ear footprints, four leg axes, tail route, eye and tusk anchors, paper highlights, and broken ground-shadow footprint.

final_elements.name: rough calf head body raised trunk and one-ear silhouette
final_elements.description: Loose graphite wraps the map into one young elephant with a rounded forehead, broad body, upward-curled trunk, and one large visible near ear while the far ear stays hidden.

final_elements.name: four sturdy legs rounded feet and one tufted tail
final_elements.description: Exactly four readable legs settle beneath the body with rounded feet while one slim tail ends in a small tuft.

final_elements.name: one gentle eye one small tusk trunk opening toenail marks and ear folds
final_elements.description: The calf gains one visible calm eye, one small tusk, the trunk opening, simple rounded toenail marks, and a few large ear-fold routes.

final_elements.name: sparse skin folds directional hatching and broken ground shadow
final_elements.description: Sparse wrinkles follow the trunk, joints, and belly while directional hatching and one broken shadow establish weight without making the calf photorealistic.

final_elements.name: layered graphite volume and open-paper highlights
final_elements.description: Broad graphite values turn the established head, ears, body, legs, trunk, and shadow while preserving open-paper highlights and visible tooth.

final_elements.name: restrained blue-gray body and dusty-rose ear pencil
final_elements.description: Light blue-gray pencil cools the established body and dusty rose warms the near-ear interior without covering the graphite texture.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: The far ear remains fully hidden behind the head, and the visible near ear overlaps only the head-and-shoulder area marked in the pale map; no finished head or body texture is drawn beneath it.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: The belly contour stops at all four reserved leg attachments, far-leg contours stop behind the two near legs, and the ground shadow stops at each planted foot.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: Graphite value and later color stop around the eye, tusk, trunk opening, toenail marks, and paper-highlight routes established in the first map.

rejection_checks: Keep one left-facing calf, one upward-curled trunk, exactly one visible ear with the far ear hidden, four legs, one visible eye, one small tusk, one tail, one crop, and one scale in all eight panels.
The trunk route, ear sizes, head-body proportion, leg order, tail position, face, folds, and shadow may not drift between panels.
Keep all four legs readable after Step 3; no leg may disappear and return, and the far pair must stay behind the near pair.
Do not add a water spray, tree, grassland scene, second elephant, extra tusk, blanket, readable text, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, or decorative border.
The final panel may not introduce an anatomy contour, ear, leg, foot, tail, eye, tusk, trunk opening, fold, shadow shape, hatch route, highlight, or color area.
The finish must retain believable graphite and colored-pencil tooth rather than photorealistic skin, glossy AI illustration, vector-clean icon art, digital gradients, or rasterized vector drawing.
